definition: Camaraderie means warm friendship and trust among a group.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word camaraderie. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know camaraderie should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: A season of muddy vans and cold pizza gave the rowing team a camaraderie the new coach could feel from the dock.
Familiarity is much weaker than camaraderie — being familiar only means the faces and habits are known, while camaraderie adds the warmth a group earns by pulling through shared work together.
Brotherhood goes further than camaraderie — the crew's warmth hardened into something lifelong, closer to family than to friendship.

Fellowship is the warm feeling of belonging to a community — a congregation, a club, a scholarly society — often gathered around a shared belief. Camaraderie is earned differently: not by believing together but by working together, through the long hours a crew puts in side by side.

Solidarity is standing together behind a cause — a unity of purpose that can bind complete strangers. Camaraderie cannot be had with strangers: it is the warm, joking trust of people who have shared work, risk, or long hours, and it has to be earned in company.
